prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room), Main Transformer (abnormal trends escalated), export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher if capability<target; Dispatcher sets permitted export; relay applies ceiling, keeps protection unless authorized switching plan). Public grid, port out of scope. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus; Lockout stays until authority confirms safe. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms→Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace→Substation Operator), Helideck. Modes: Substation Degraded, Grid Constraint, Weather Hold, Vessel Standby. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard). Alarms safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway), Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; holds last validated limit on grid comms loss; Switching Window Acknowledgment; incident log; tracks go/no-go decisions and restrictions), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale; replenishment forecasts from demand and criticality), Work Permit Portal (Isolation Boundary Sketch), Operations Radio Console, Personnel Tracking Console. Weather Analyst: Wave Burst Record; Visibility Confidence Note→Duty Planner; low confidence constrains; point estimate cannot authorize. No-go if safety cannot be demonstrated; reassess on current evidence before resuming. Marine Coordinator: Berth Slot Confirmation, vessel assignment, approach plans; reassesses route with Vessel Master as uncertainty grows. Vessel Master: Transfer Manifest Addendum; Crew Count Correction→Personnel Tracking Console; authority to proceed, slow, divert or hold. Crew Transfer Vessel kept clear until visual awareness; Daughter Craft caution; Service Operations Vessel stand-off; Recovery Basket Load Sheet→Rescue Coordinator. Inventory: Warehouse System is authoritative catalogue, balances, locations, reservations (no double allocation); Spares Hub regional/emergency stock; Storekeeper reconciles counts, logs adjustments with reason and timestamp; serial traceability. Duty Planner checks stock before readiness. Priority: safety-critical/restoration parts, then window-protecting

New part:
S699: Replenishment requests include the required quantity, need date, delivery location, and applicable handling requirements.
S700: Supplier lead times are reviewed against recent delivery performance rather than relying solely on catalogue estimates.
S701: Low-stock alerts identify items approaching their reorder point and show open purchase commitments.
S702: A shortage that threatens a work window is escalated to the Duty Planner for a priority decision.
S703: The Storekeeper records unavailable quantities and the expected date of the next supply without presenting them as available stock.
S704: Substitutions require engineering acceptance and confirmation that the alternative meets the required interface and operating limits.
S705: Damaged, suspect, or expired parts are segregated from usable stock until their status is resolved.
S706: A count discrepancy is investigated against receipts, issues, reservations, and recent movements before the balance is corrected.
S707: Urgent purchases require documented authorization and retain the same traceability and inspection controls as routine receipts.
S708: During transport, the dispatch record identifies the quantity, destination, handling conditions, and responsible receiving location.
S709: Returned parts are inspected and their condition is recorded before they are restored to available stock.
S710: Repeated delays, shortages, and count discrepancies are reviewed to adjust reorder levels and supplier priorities.
S711: An isolation boundary defines the equipment and energy sources that must be made safe before field work begins.
S712: The boundary is approved against the task scope, current equipment configuration, and applicable operating constraints.
S713: The Work Permit Portal makes the approved boundary available to the work party and the control team.
S714: The approval identifies each isolation point, the required device position, and the person responsible for applying the control.
S715: It also records any adjacent equipment that must remain energized or available for service.
S716: The Electrical Technician uses the boundary sketch to identify the approved isolation points before starting the work.
S717: The Field Supervisor briefs the crew on the boundary, access restrictions, and conditions that require work to stop.
S718: The Control Engineer checks that remote indications agree with the approved switching state before authorizing access.
S719: Where local indication is required, a qualified technician checks the device at the point of isolation.
S720: The work party confirms equipment identity using permanent labels and the current site designation.
S721: A mismatch between the field label and the approved record prevents the crew from proceeding until it is resolved.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
